description: Relation type definitions for pancreatic cancer biomedical relation extraction. Based on BioRED relation taxonomy (Luo et al., 2022) with directionality from BioREDirect (Lai et al., 2025). Covers ALL biomedical relation types found in pancreatic cancer literature.

Positive_Correlation.description: Entity A positively affects, increases, induces, activates, upregulates, promotes, or causes entity B. The subject entity drives or enhances the object entity.

pancreatic_cancer_examples.subject: KRASG12D
pancreatic_cancer_examples.sentence: KRAS G12D mutation drives pancreatic cancer progression

pancreatic_cancer_examples.subject: gemcitabine
pancreatic_cancer_examples.sentence: Gemcitabine treatment induced peripheral neuropathy (adverse effect)

pancreatic_cancer_examples.subject: KRAS
pancreatic_cancer_examples.sentence: Oncogenic KRAS activates the MAPK signaling pathway

pancreatic_cancer_examples.subject: Hedgehog pathway
pancreatic_cancer_examples.sentence: Hedgehog pathway activation promotes chemoresistance in PDAC

pancreatic_cancer_examples.subject: c-Myc
pancreatic_cancer_examples.sentence: c-Myc overexpression increased proliferation in PANC-1 cells

Negative_Correlation.description: Entity A negatively affects, decreases, inhibits, suppresses, downregulates, treats, or blocks entity B. The subject entity reduces or counteracts the object entity.

pancreatic_cancer_examples.subject: gemcitabine
pancreatic_cancer_examples.sentence: Gemcitabine is used as first-line treatment for pancreatic cancer

pancreatic_cancer_examples.subject: olaparib
pancreatic_cancer_examples.sentence: Olaparib inhibits PARP enzyme activity

pancreatic_cancer_examples.subject: erlotinib
pancreatic_cancer_examples.sentence: Erlotinib suppresses EGFR signaling

pancreatic_cancer_examples.subject: saikosaponin D
pancreatic_cancer_examples.sentence: SSD overcomes gemcitabine resistance via AKT/mTOR pathway inhibition

pancreatic_cancer_examples.subject: SMAD4
pancreatic_cancer_examples.sentence: SMAD4 suppresses angiogenesis in PDAC

Association.description: General association between two entities where the specific directional mechanism is not stated or is ambiguous. Use when the text establishes a link but does not specify positive or negative correlation. Includes biomarker associations, prognostic associations, and general co-occurrence with stated relevance.

pancreatic_cancer_examples.subject: CA19-9
pancreatic_cancer_examples.sentence: CA19-9 is associated with pancreatic cancer prognosis

pancreatic_cancer_examples.subject: KRAS
pancreatic_cancer_examples.sentence: KRAS mutations are found in ~94% of PDAC cases

pancreatic_cancer_examples.subject: PD-L1
pancreatic_cancer_examples.sentence: PD-L1 expression was correlated with immune cell infiltration

pancreatic_cancer_examples.subject: gemcitabine
pancreatic_cancer_examples.sentence: Response to gemcitabine was associated with BRCA2 mutation status

Binding.description: Physical molecular binding or direct interaction between two entities. Includes receptor-ligand binding, protein-protein physical interaction, drug-target binding, and complex formation.

pancreatic_cancer_examples.subject: erlotinib
pancreatic_cancer_examples.sentence: Erlotinib binds to the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain

pancreatic_cancer_examples.subject: PD-1
pancreatic_cancer_examples.sentence: PD-1 binds to PD-L1 on tumor cells

pancreatic_cancer_examples.subject: olaparib
pancreatic_cancer_examples.sentence: Olaparib directly binds the PARP catalytic site

Drug_Interaction.description: Pharmacological interaction between two drugs/chemicals when co-administered. The combined effect differs from individual effects. Includes synergistic, antagonistic, and additive drug interactions.

pancreatic_cancer_examples.subject: olaparib
pancreatic_cancer_examples.sentence: Olaparib has synergistic effects with gemcitabine in PDAC cells

pancreatic_cancer_examples.subject: evofosfamide
pancreatic_cancer_examples.sentence: Evofosfamide and gemcitabine act synergistically in pancreatic cancer

Cotreatment.description: Two drugs/chemicals used together as a combined treatment regimen. Unlike Drug_Interaction (which describes pharmacological mechanism), Cotreatment describes clinical co-administration.

pancreatic_cancer_examples.subject: gemcitabine
pancreatic_cancer_examples.sentence: Patients received gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel as first-line treatment

pancreatic_cancer_examples.subject: ceralasertib
pancreatic_cancer_examples.sentence: Sequential ATR (ceralasertib) and PARP (olaparib) inhibition overcomes resistance

Comparison.description: Two entities (typically drugs or treatments) are explicitly compared in a study. The comparison may or may not determine superiority.

pancreatic_cancer_examples.subject: FOLFIRINOX
pancreatic_cancer_examples.sentence: FOLFIRINOX showed superior survival compared to gemcitabine alone

pancreatic_cancer_examples.subject: olaparib
pancreatic_cancer_examples.sentence: Olaparib maintenance versus placebo in BRCA-mutated PDAC

Conversion.description: One chemical/compound is metabolized or converted into another. Includes prodrug activation and metabolic transformations.

pancreatic_cancer_examples.subject: 5-FU
pancreatic_cancer_examples.sentence: Capecitabine is an oral prodrug of 5-fluorouracil

pancreatic_cancer_examples.subject: evofosfamide
pancreatic_cancer_examples.sentence: Evofosfamide is a hypoxia-activated prodrug

Novel.description: The relation describes a NEW finding, result, conclusion, or observation reported by the current study. The relation is part of what the authors discovered or demonstrated.

Known.description: The relation describes PREVIOUSLY PUBLISHED background knowledge cited or assumed by the authors. The relation is not a new finding of the current study.

no_relation_handling: Only annotate positive (existing) relations. Entity pairs that co-occur in the same sentence without an annotated relation are implicitly treated as 'No Relation' during model training.
design_rationale: The relation schema directly follows BioRED (Luo et al., 2022) to ensure comparability with the established benchmark. All 8 BioRED relation types are retained: Positive_Correlation, Negative_Correlation, and Association cover ~96% of relations; Binding, Drug_Interaction, Cotreatment, Comparison, and Conversion cover specialized interactions. Directionality follows BioREDirect (Lai et al., 2025) — subject/object roles are annotated for directed relations. The Novel/Known distinction is adopted from BioRED to enable identification of new discoveries versus background knowledge. This schema was validated against 30 sampled PanCan-RE abstracts and the corpus-wide relation signal analysis showing all 8 types are represented in the data.
